findings.title: Model-assisted raw-response envelopes accept schema/type/additional-property drift
findings.claim: The hash-pinned model-assisted response envelope is not validated as a strict schema. An envelope with schemaVersion set to an array and an unexpected top-level property is accepted when its nested review payload matches the sealed lane artifact.

evidence.detail: validate_reviewer strict-parses the JSON and manually compares selected provenance fields, then returns body.review. It does not check schemaVersion, an exact key set/additionalProperties, stream, format, responseCreatedAt, done, or doneReason, and no model-envelope schema is present in SCHEMA_PATHS.

steps: Start from the passing one-unit mutation fixture.
Use a model-assisted blind reviewer and write a hash-pinned ollama-cloud-audit-review envelope whose nested review exactly equals the sealed blind payload.
Set the outer schemaVersion to [] and add unexpectedAdditionalProperty.
Recompute the response and lane-chain hashes, then invoke validate().
reproduction.expected: Strict schema/type/additional-property validation should return a normal validation failure.

findings.minimalFix: Define and apply a strict model-response-envelope schema (or an equivalent exact-key/type contract) before reading body.review. Require schemaVersion 1 and all success/provenance fields with additionalProperties false; return a validation failure without consuming review when the envelope is invalid. Add focused wrong-type, missing-key, and additional-property tests.

findings.title: Schema-invalid ID/reference/severity values can crash validation
findings.claim: Artifact schema errors are recorded but semantic validation continues over the malformed values. Lists placed where strings are required reach set construction or set-membership operations and raise TypeError instead of producing a fail-closed validation report.

evidence.detail: validate_packet applies the schema and then unconditionally executes set(packet_ids) and set(row.auditUnitIds).
validate_blind unconditionally hashes auditUnitId values in set(result_ids) and packet evidenceId values in a set comprehension after schema validation.
validate_comparison tests severity against a set and converts evidenceRefs to a set without first proving those values hashable strings.

Six independent malformed-type probes crashed with TypeError: unhashable type: list: comparison severity, packet auditUnitId, packet evidence auditUnitId, packet evidenceId, blind auditUnitId, and comparison evidenceRef.

reproduction.observed: Each case raised TypeError: unhashable type: list from validate(); the control passed with zero failures.
reproduction.expected: Each schema-invalid value should return passed false with one or more explanatory failures and no exception.

findings.minimalFix: Stop semantic validation of an artifact when apply_schema returns false, or normalize every semantic consumer to validated string-only values before hashing/membership. Preserve the schema failures in the returned report. Add non-crashing mutation controls for every ID, reference-list, enum, and dictionary-key path, not only discrepancyId and verification reviewId.

scopeChecks.detail: Candidate 1's passing control still passed after the comparator raw response was replaced with hash-pinned {unrelated: true}. Both validation runs had zero failures.

scopeChecks.topic: Exact substantive response binding on current candidate
scopeChecks.detail: All eight exact controls passed and all eight unrelated-nonempty controls failed exactly once across completeness, blind, comparison, and verification lanes for both agent and model-assisted envelopes.
A duplicate unitResults key in an agent raw response failed strict parsing, and a duplicate schemaVersion key in a comparison artifact failed strict parsing.

scopeChecks.topic: Strict artifact additional-property and ordinary type failures
scopeChecks.detail: Unexpected properties in packet, completeness, blind, comparison, and result artifacts each produced a normal schema failure. A wrong-type blind behavior also produced a normal schema failure. Wrong-type comparison severity and several malformed ID/reference shapes crash as S5-002; malformed model outer-envelope drift passes as S5-001.

candidateDiffAssessment.detail: The candidate adds exact payload comparisons for completeness, blind, comparison, and verification. The focused current-candidate probe confirms those comparisons for agent and model-assisted responses. Strict outer model-envelope validation and general schema-invalid crash resistance remain incomplete.

testsRun.detail: Byte-checked 1,098 files in docs/rulebooks and assets/tts-mod/extract in the assigned worktree; zero copies were needed.
73/73 committed controls passed; the suite has only narrow unhashable discrepancyId and verification reviewId coverage and therefore does not expose S5-002's other crashing paths.
On candidate 5e525e12c105edb7565fa310ae16a526bc131025, both the control and the hash-pinned unrelated comparator-response mutation passed, reproducing JSON-001.

34 focused cases: control passed; strict duplicate/additional-property controls passed; eight exact binding controls passed; eight unrelated-nonempty binding mutations failed; six malformed-type/ID cases crashed; malformed outer model envelope passed.

externalArtifacts.purpose: Bounded current-candidate specialty probe outside the assigned repository.
Bounded JSON-001 reproduction against superseded candidate 1.
This final rereview report outside Git.

residualRisks: The focused probes cover representative malformed values and all four substantive binding lanes, not every schema leaf. S5-002's root pattern implies additional unhashable or structurally wrong values may crash unless schema failure becomes a hard semantic-validation boundary.
This is a prelock harness review. No claim is made about future reviewer content beyond the validator behavior exercised here.
